summary: Fort Bliss is a large United States Army post spanning New Mexico and Texas, with its headquarters in El Paso, Texas. The note describes its size, its naming after LTC William Bliss, its role as the largest FORSCOM installation, and its extensive restricted airspace and maneuver areas used for training and testing.
one_line: Fort Bliss is a vast U.S. Army post in New Mexico and Texas, headquartered in El Paso, known for its huge training airspace and maneuver areas.
key_facts: Fort Bliss is a United States Army post in the U.S. states of New Mexico and Texas.
The headquarters of Fort Bliss is located in El Paso, Texas.
Fort Bliss is named in honor of LTC William Bliss (1815 - 1853).
William Bliss was described as a mathematical genius and was the son-in-law of President Zachary Taylor.
Fort Bliss has an area of about 1,700 square miles (4,400 km).
Fort Bliss is the largest installation in FORSCOM (United States Army Forces Command).
Fort Bliss is the second-largest installation in the Army overall, with the largest being the adjacent White Sands Missile Range.
The portion of Fort Bliss located in El Paso County, Texas, is a census-designated place with a population of 8,591 as of the 2010 census.
Fort Bliss provides the largest contiguous tract of restricted airspace in the Continental United States, about 1,500 sq mi (3,900 km).
The restricted airspace at Fort Bliss is used for missile and artillery training and testing.
Fort Bliss boasts the largest maneuver area at 992,000 acres.
The National Training Center has 642,000 acres, which is smaller than the Fort Bliss maneuver area.
